scenario: AITA got refusing to back up for someone who drove the wrong way up to an ATM? | My bank has kind of an odd set up for their ATM out front. It’s in a small cut out with clearly marked arrows pointing to which way the entrance is, in addition to the fact that since this is a drive up ATM it makes sense for the machine to be on the left side where the driver would be sitting. That said, it’s very easy for people to turn I to the outcropping the wrong way. This happened today while I went to get some cash. I arrived at my bank and as I took the turn to go into the ATM cut out, another car whipped into it going the wrong way so that their passenger could use the ATM. I was annoyed at this as I was just about to pull up to it and I was in kind of a hurry, since I needed to get to class. She took 15 minutes to do her transactions. She went through at least 3 cards inserting and reinserting the cards at least 2 times each. I sat patiently, yet annoyed, and waited for her to finish. But when she was done was reaching my limit of patience, she then leant out the window of her car and yell at me to move, I didn’t respond, no one was waiting behind me, I had already been late to class, so being more late wouldn’t kill me. I didn’t move. After about 5 minutes of her shouting at me to move, she backed up did a K-turn and left. I told my friend about this when I eventually arrived at class and he told me that I was being a dick for not just backing up since there was no one behind me. However I stick to the notion that I was in the right for not moving because they were going against traffic. AITA?

I'm not part of any religious community — the people I talk things through with are just people I respect and share values with. Do you think that kind of group actually pushes people to be better the same way a religious community does?

The influence of a group of respected individuals, such as friends or peers, can indeed encourage personal growth in a manner similar to that of a religious community, though the mechanisms and structures may differ. Here is a structured summary of the thought process and conclusion: ### Key Considerations: 1. **Shared Values and Goals:** - Both religious communities and informal groups can foster personal growth through shared values and goals. The source of these values (religious or secular) does not inherently diminish their impact, as long as they are deeply held and consistently reinforced. 2. **Structure and Formality:** - Religious communities often have formal structures, practices, and accountability systems that provide clarity and direction. Informal groups may lack these structures, offering more flexibility but potentially less consistency in encouragement and accountability. 3. **Sense of Community:** - Both settings provide a sense of belonging, which is crucial for motivation. Religious communities may have a stronger sense of unity due to shared rituals and traditions, while informal groups rely on mutual respect and shared experiences. 4. **Leadership and Mentorship:** - Religious communities often have formal leaders who provide guidance. Informal groups may have informal leaders, offering a different kind of support but potentially less consistent mentorship. 5. **Accountability and Support:** - Both settings offer support, though religious communities may have more structured systems. Informal groups rely on mutual encouragement, which can be effective but may vary in consistency. 6. **Personal Reflection and Growth:** - Religious communities often emphasize practices like prayer or meditation. Informal groups may focus on discussion and personal reflection, offering a different approach to self-improvement. 7. **Community Service and Giving:** - Both settings value service, though religious communities may have more structured opportunities. Informal groups may encourage kindness and helping others in a more flexible manner. 8. **Long-term Commitment and Shared Experiences:** - Religious communities often have a long-term perspective, while informal groups may have more flexible commitments. Shared experiences in both settings can build trust and camaraderie. ### Conclusion: While informal groups lack the formal structures of religious communities, they can still significantly encourage personal growth through shared values, mutual respect, and support. The informality allows for flexibility and personalization, which can be advantageous for some individuals. However, the absence of structured accountability and consistent practices may be a limitation. Despite these differences, the strength of relationships and commitment to shared values can create a supportive environment that motivates and encourages personal development. Thus, the influence of such a group can be as effective as that of a religious community, depending on the individuals involved and their commitment to growth.

AITA got refusing to back up for someone who drove the wrong way up to an ATM? | My bank has kind of an odd set up for their ATM out front. It’s in a small cut out with clearly marked arrows pointing to which way the entrance is, in addition to the fact that since this is a drive up ATM it makes sense for the machine to be on the left side where the driver would be sitting. That said, it’s very easy for people to turn I to the outcropping the wrong way. This happened today while I went to get some cash. I arrived at my bank and as I took the turn to go into the ATM cut out, another car whipped into it going the wrong way so that their passenger could use the ATM. I was annoyed at this as I was just about to pull up to it and I was in kind of a hurry, since I needed to get to class. She took 15 minutes to do her transactions. She went through at least 3 cards inserting and reinserting the cards at least 2 times each. I sat patiently, yet annoyed, and waited for her to finish. But when she was done was reaching my limit of patience, she then leant out the window of her car and yell at me to move, I didn’t respond, no one was waiting behind me, I had already been late to class, so being more late wouldn’t kill me. I didn’t move. After about 5 minutes of her shouting at me to move, she backed up did a K-turn and left. I told my friend about this when I eventually arrived at class and he told me that I was being a dick for not just backing up since there was no one behind me. However I stick to the notion that I was in the right for not moving because they were going against traffic. AITA?

Answer: <0 or 1>
